name: Arizona
note: The funeral establishment or responsible person who takes possession of the remains completes the death certificate, including the SSN, and submits it (electronically allowed) within seven calendar days; a local or state registrar registers it within 72 hours. The treating health care provider, the facility's designated provider, or the medical examiner signs the medical certification within 72 hours, and the funeral establishment needs a disposition-transit permit before final disposition. Each month the Department of Health Services sends the secretary of state a record of every resident's death, which drives voter cancellation by county recorders. Certified copies go only to persons eligible under rule, funeral directors and government agencies.

steps.title: Health care institution contacts the responsible person before releasing remains
steps.who: The health care institution where the death occurred, to the responsible person (the person with the right to control disposition under § 36-831).
steps.trigger: A death in a health care institution.
steps.summary: The institution may not release the remains until it has made a diligent effort to reach the responsible person and learn which entity will receive them. No Arizona statute read names who may pronounce death.

steps.title: Report listed deaths to a peace officer / medical examiner
steps.who: Any person with knowledge of the death.
steps.trigger: Death not under current care of a provider, violent, unexpected or unexplained, in custody, unexpected child death, suspicious or occupational, during anaesthesia or surgery, a public-health disease, or an unidentified body.
steps.summary: The medical examiner then certifies the cause. Knowingly failing to report a death to a peace officer is a class 1 misdemeanour under § 36-344.

steps.title: Treating provider or facility designee signs the medical certification
steps.who: The health care provider (physician, naturopath, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, midwife and others in § 36-301) treating the condition that caused death; for natural deaths in hospitals, nursing homes and hospices, a provider the facility designates.
steps.trigger: Request to complete the death certificate.
steps.summary: If no provider had current care of the decedent, the medical examiner certifies instead. Providers who sign in good faith are immune from civil liability and discipline.

steps.title: Medical examiner signs the medical certification
steps.who: The county medical examiner or alternate medical examiner; tribal law enforcement on a reservation without a medical examiner.

deadline.text: within seventy-two hours after the examination, excluding weekends and holidays

steps.summary: Where the cause cannot yet be determined, 'pending' is entered and registration proceeds; disposition waits for the medical examiner's release.

steps.title: Funeral establishment submits the death certificate
steps.who: The funeral establishment or responsible person who takes possession of the remains.

deadline.text: within seven calendar days after receiving possession of human remains

steps.summary: The certificate, including the decedent's SSN, is submitted to a local or state registrar and may be filed electronically. Disregarding a duty under the chapter is a class 3 misdemeanour.

steps.title: Registrar registers the certificate
steps.who: A local registrar, deputy local registrar or the state registrar.
steps.trigger: Receipt of an accurate and complete death certificate.

deadline.text: within seventy-two hours after receiving a death certificate

steps.summary: Registration takes place within 72 hours of receipt.

steps.title: Disposition-transit permit before final disposition
steps.who: The funeral establishment or responsible person in possession of the remains.
steps.trigger: Before final disposition or moving the remains out of Arizona.
steps.summary: The permit is issued when the information provided complies with the chapter and rules; the statute does not expressly require prior registration of the death certificate. Transporting or accepting remains without the accompanying permit is a misdemeanour.

steps.title: Certified copies to rule-eligible persons and funeral directors
steps.who: Persons eligible under ADHS rules, and the licensed funeral director or designee.
steps.summary: A registrar issues certified copies without medical information to applicants eligible under rule criteria; eligibility details are in the Arizona Administrative Code, which could not be reached.

steps.title: Government agencies get copies of or access to vital records
steps.who: Any government agency, for its official purposes.
steps.summary: The state registrar must provide agencies a copy of, or access to, vital records for their official purposes.

steps.title: ADHS sends monthly resident death records to the secretary of state
steps.who: The Department of Health Services, without charge; records include the SSN where available. An annual record of all reported resident deaths is also provided.
steps.trigger: Deaths reported to the department in the preceding month.
steps.summary: The secretary of state matches the records against the statewide voter registration database and notifies the county recorder.

steps.title: County recorder cancels the deceased voter's registration
steps.who: The county recorder, on notice from the secretary of state or other information it confirms.
steps.trigger: Notice and confirmation of the registrant's death.
steps.summary: Death is a statutory cause for cancelling registration once the recorder is informed and confirms it.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Seven calendar days from the funeral establishment receiving possession of the remains (not from death); registration then within 72 hours of receipt.

informantDuty.note: The funeral establishment, or the responsible person who takes possession of the remains, completes and submits the certificate.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate; the medical examiner certifies only reported deaths and those without a provider in current care.

electronicRegistration.note: Electronic submission of the certificate is permitted, not mandated, in § 36-325.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the state registrar keeps vital records and gives agencies access for official purposes.

governmentPropagation.note: Registered resident deaths go monthly to the secretary of state for voter cancellation; other agencies are entitled to access on request. No statutory death feed to the Motor Vehicle Division, Department of Revenue or AHCCCS was found. Federal feeds are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Certified copies only to persons eligible under rule criteria, funeral directors and agencies.

gaps: Rechecked 28 October 2026: all 13 quotes were compared character for character against the raw statute pages, fetched from azleg.gov with a plain request (no Sucuri challenge was served), and each appears verbatim in the section its citation names.

The Arizona Administrative Code (R9-19, eligibility for certified death certificates, and any public-after-50-years rule) is on apps.azsos.gov, which is outside the session's network allowlist (CONNECT 403 / DNS failure); azsos.gov and www.azdhs.gov are also blocked.
privateSectorVerification is left to the us-federal layer (LADMF); no Arizona-law verification route for banks or insurers was found.
No statute naming who may pronounce death was found; § 36-325 refers to the place where death was pronounced without saying who pronounces.

§ 16-165(H) requires county recorders to compare voter rolls with an SSA database monthly 'to the extent practicable', but the text read does not say it is death data, so it is not recorded as a step.
No statutory death feed to the Motor Vehicle Division (Title 28), Department of Revenue, or AHCCCS was searched for or found.
Whether ADHS's electronic vital records system transmits to SSA is not stated in the sections read; the federal side belongs in us-federal.
